Hi Sofia / Tony — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap of what we covered and the concrete next steps so everyone is aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary from call:
- Data types in scope: conversational logs (chat transcripts), user metadata (name/email), and derived embeddings tied to user ids.
- RTBF trigger model: customer-initiated delete request (UI/API) -> Redwood triggers removal from active stores -> downstream snapshot/backups follow policy.
- Restore window: you asked whether we can support a 30-day restore window for customer-level restores and whether that affects deletion timelines.
- Backups: Acme currently retains monthly snapshots for 13 months (per your note). You asked if Redwood can guarantee removal from those snapshots.

Open questions we need to confirm from your side:
1) Target deletion SLA for active data (e.g., 48 hours, 7 days?) and whether you require a certificate of destruction for compliance.
2) Are there legal/contractual holds that require snapshot preservation beyond typical retention (e.g., litigation hold)?
3) Do you require KMS key handback or key destruction when we purge customer data?

What we propose / next steps (internal + customer):
- I attached a draft "ACME_RTBF_Timeline_v1.xlsx" that maps steps (active store sweep, index removal, cache flush, backup overwrite request) with target windows.
- Redwood action items: 1) confirm active-store purge time (we typically do a logical delete followed by physical purge within 48–72h); 2) verify backup overwrite process with infra provider and surface expected overwrite window (provider-dependent); 3) provide an audit log extract and export format for your audits.
- Please confirm: (a) desired SLA for active deletion, (b) whether snapshots must be retained beyond 90 days, and (c) if you need a signed attestation when deletion completes.

Attachments: ACME_RTBF_Timeline_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), backup-retention-overview.pdf (provider excerpt)

Thanks — happy to set a short follow-up with Privacy/Infra if useful.

Hi Sofia / Tony — thanks for the questions. Monica and Ben reviewed; below are the short answers and a proposed operational timeline so you can decide what to include in the SOW. Happy to run through live if useful.

1) Backups / snapshots
- What we can commit to: Redwood will initiate an expedited overwrite request for provider-managed snapshots immediately after RTBF completion. For application-layer data and customer-owned backups we control, we will complete logical and physical purges within 60 days in the standard plan.
- Provider limitations: If snapshots are retained by the infra provider (e.g., monthly immutable snapshots at the block level), removal timing is provider-dependent. Typical maximum measured window for full overwrite/garbage-collection is 45–90 days — we see variability across providers and regions. We recommend contracting a 90-day maximum for snapshot overwrite exceptions, or optionally longer if Acme's infra policy requires 13-month retention.

2) Audit evidence
- We can provide a machine-readable deletion log (JSONL) that includes: deletion_event_id, timestamp (UTC), customer_id, data_types_removed, actor (Redwood action id). We can also provide a signed attestation in PDF form upon bulk deletion.

3) Request-level logs & pseudonymization
- Default: request-level logs are retained unredacted for 90 days. Long-term logs (beyond 90 days) are pseudonymized; payload fields containing PII are redacted. We can offer a stricter policy as part of an enterprise contract to reduce the unredacted window.

4) Customer-managed KMS
- For BYOK: Redwood does not perform key destruction. If Acme disables or destroys its KMS key, restoration from encrypted backups becomes infeasible. We can document the key lifecycle steps in the SOW and include the option for Acme to request a key escrow/rotation window prior to deletion.

Proposed timeline (draft) — see attached spreadsheet for mapping to actions:
- Day 0: RTBF request accepted (ticket created)
- 0–48h: Logical delete from active stores; mark user ids for purge; invalidate KV caches and live indexes
- 48h–7 days: Physical purge of application-layer objects (dependent on object store GC)
- 7–60 days: Backup overwrite/expedite request; if infra provider enforces monthly immutable snapshots, final purge may take up to 90 days
- Post completion: Redwood provides deletion JSONL export + signed attestation within 5 business days of final purge

Next steps:
- Please confirm whether Acme will accept the proposed 90-day maximum for provider-managed snapshot overwrite. If not, we should capture the specific retention exception in the contract and discuss whether Acme will accept a separate archival/hold process.
- If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute session with our Privacy Ops and Infra teams this week to walk through the technical constraints and wording to put into the SOW.
